The `source` array uses a predictable URL constructed from `_ghurl`, `pkgver`, and `CARCH`, which is common practice for AUR packages fetching prebuilt binaries. There are no attempts to download, exfiltrate, or execute code at parse time.

All variables are statically defined or derived from other static values. No network operations or dangerous expansions occur in the global scope. The use of `${CARCH}` in the source URL is normal and handled safely by makepkg. Even though the checksum is provided and matches a binary RPM (which is typical for `-bin` packages), its presence or absence has no impact on this phase. Since nothing malicious executes during sourcing, this PKGBUILD passes the narrow safety gate for `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
</details>

The provided `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR packaging system and does not contain executable code. It describes the package `rowel-bin`, including its version, dependencies, source URL, and checksum. The source is a prebuilt RPM package hosted on the official GitHub releases page of the project (`https://github.com/fwdai/rowel/releases`), which is consistent with the application's upstream. The `sha256sums` field contains a valid checksum that matches the expected integrity of the source file, indicating that the package maintainer has verified the release artifact.

There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious network locations, or unexpected scripts. The use of a binary RPM as source is typical for `-bin` packages in AUR, and while such packages inherently require more trust in the upstream provider, this does not constitute a supply-chain attack in itself. The source URL points directly to a specific tagged release (`v1.0.0`), which is a pinned and immutable reference, enhancing reproducibility.

No dangerous operations (e.g., dynamic downloads during build, execution of fetched code, or data exfiltration) are described or implied in this file. As `.SRCINFO` is not executed and only serves as a package metadata descriptor, and given that all referenced sources are from the project's official repository, the file presents no evidence of malicious intent.
</details>

The `prepare()` function modifies the desktop file to set a category and moves a high-DPI icon directory to a standard path, both benign adjustments. The `package()` function installs the binary, icons, and desktop file with appropriate permissions.

The source URL points to a legitimate upstream release (`https://github.com/fwdai/rowel`), and the SHA-256 checksum is provided and matches the expected value for the release asset. There are no network requests outside of the declared source, no use of `eval`, `base64`, or obfuscated payloads, and no execution of downloaded code during build. The dependencies are standard for a GUI application using WebKit. Icon renaming and desktop file patching are common practices in AUR packaging to ensure proper integration.

While the package uses a prebuilt binary (which limits auditability of the actual application code), the packaging script itself does not introduce additional risks. The actions taken in the PKGBUILD align with standard AUR packaging practices and serve only to integrate the upstream binary into Arch Linux properly. No data exfiltration, remote code execution, or unauthorized system modifications are present.
</details>
